newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHARP-EYED FAN SAVES DERBY FROM PUNISHMENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHARP-EYED FAN SAVES DERBY FROM PUNISHMENT.

text.p: Derby came within minutes of fielding too many non-EU players in an English premier league match on Wednesday before being saved from a possible points deduction by a sharp-eyed fan.
Derby manager Jim Smith had named four non-European Union players -- one more than the permitted maximum -- in his side to face Nottingham Forest at the Baseball Ground.
A supporter spotted the error and alerted the Derby bench just before kick-off.
Smith replaced Estonian goalkeeper Mart Poom with locally-born substitute keeper Russell Hoult and the match went ahead as scheduled, ending in a 0-0 draw.
"If it hadn't been spotted we would have faced some sort of punishment, possibly the docking of a league point," Smith said.
